evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.intro: Does the stress signal agree with what satellites saw on this field? Each year, modelled water stress is compared with how green the vegetation was against its own average.
evidence.noField.body: The back-test compares the climate record and satellite vegetation record of a specific location.
evidence.error.title: Could not load the back-test
evidence.empty.title: No years to compare
evidence.empty.body: The back-test returned no years with both a stress value and a vegetation value for this location.
evidence.baseline.title: Demo data: the published back-test for the Denizli demo field
evidence.baseline.body: The engine did not provide a back-test for this request, so this page shows the contract fixture: the engine's back-test for the demo field (37.89° N, 28.98° E) as published in docs/VALIDATION.md. It is not computed for the field you selected.
evidence.r.title: Correlation
evidence.r.negative: Negative: in years with more modelled stress, the vegetation was usually less green than its average. That is the direction a useful stress signal should show.
evidence.r.positive: Positive: in years with more modelled stress, the vegetation was usually greener than its average. That is the opposite of what a useful stress signal should show.
evidence.r.zero: Zero: no linear relationship between modelled stress and vegetation in these years.
evidence.r.scale: r runs from −1 to 1. Values near 0 mean little linear relationship; values near −1 or 1 mean the two series move closely together.
evidence.chart.title: Modelled stress against observed vegetation
evidence.chart.subtitle: {from}–{to} · n = {n} · {datasets}
evidence.chart.aria: Back-test from {from} to {to}: modelled stress and observed NDVI anomaly for {n} years, correlation r = {r}.
evidence.readout.hint: Hover or focus the chart and use the arrow keys to read each year.
evidence.language: The method and caveats are shown in English, exactly as the engine returns them.

ndvi30.title: Field-scale greenness, 30 m (HLS), by growing season
ndvi30.why: The 250 m MODIS pixel also covers land around the field, while the 30 m HLS pixel lies inside it, so the two describe different areas: compare years within one column, not values across columns.
ndvi30.error: Could not load the 30 m vegetation record
ndvi30.empty: No growing season with clear 30 m observations for this location.
ndvi30.demo: Demo data: the engine's 30 m record for the demo field.

evidence.compare.title: Model against a simple baseline
evidence.compare.subtitle: Pearson r with the NDVI anomaly and 95 % bootstrap intervals · n = {n}
evidence.compare.rule: Rule fixed before the results (docs/VALIDATION.md): the model is called better only if the whole interval of the difference lies below 0.
evidence.verdict.model_better: The model's correlation is more negative than the baseline's and the difference is outside the noise.
evidence.verdict.baseline_better: The baseline's correlation is more negative than the model's and the difference is outside the noise.
evidence.verdict.no_detectable_differenc: No detectable difference between the model and the baseline: the interval of the difference includes 0.

landing.problem.title: The problem
landing.problem.body: Farms in dry regions such as the Büyük Menderes basin face hotter and more variable growing seasons. Which crops to grow, and in what order, decides how much water a field needs and how often it runs short. Long climate and satellite records exist for every field on Earth, but they are rarely turned into an answer for one specific field.
landing.how.title: How it works
landing.how.mark.title: Mark the field
landing.how.mark.body: Draw it on the map or drop a point. The location goes into the link, so the view can be shared.
landing.how.read.title: Read its record
landing.how.read.body: Daily NASA POWER weather since 2001, FAO-56 reference evapotranspiration, SoilGrids soil and MODIS vegetation for that location.
landing.how.rank.title: Compare rotations
landing.how.rank.body: Every rotation is replayed through a daily FAO-56 soil-water balance over past seasons and ranked by what matters to you.
landing.evidence.title: Checked against the satellite record
landing.evidence.body: For the demo field near Sarayköy, Denizli, modelled water stress was compared with observed vegetation greenness for {span} (n = {n} years), under a protocol fixed before any result was computed.
landing.evidence.link: See the full back-test, method and caveats
landing.data.title: Data sources
landing.src.power: Daily weather and solar radiation since 2001 (NASA Langley Research Center), 0.5° × 0.625° grid.
landing.src.modis: Growing-season vegetation greenness (NDVI) at 250 m (NASA LP DAAC).
landing.src.soil: Soil texture, organic carbon, pH and available water at 250 m (ISRIC).
landing.src.fao: Reference evapotranspiration and crop coefficients (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56).
landing.limits.title: What it cannot tell you
landing.limits.grid: Weather is an average over a grid cell of about 55 × 55 km, not a measurement in your field.
landing.limits.soil: Soil values are model predictions for a 250 m pixel with wide uncertainty; your own soil test is better.
landing.limits.pixel: The vegetation check uses one 250 m pixel whose land use is unknown, and so far one site.
landing.limits.past: Every number is replayed from past weather. Travertine makes no forecast of future climate.
landing.limits.yield: Scores compare rotations with each other; they are not yield or price forecasts.
landing.team.title: Team
landing.ai: Built with Claude Code (Anthropic) coding agents under human review: one for the web app, one for the engine. Humans review every change before it is merged. The full statement is in docs/AI_USE.md.
